summary: Evaluation of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS profile data shows an 86.0% time-in-range, with time above range at 8.9% and time below range at 5.1%. The system operates with zero manual carb entries, relying entirely on UAM and SMB automation combined with a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U and aggressive overnight targets of 90 mg/dL, which contribute to mild nocturnal/early-morning hypoglycemia and afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7% over 14 days with good data quality and 10 minor gaps. Treatment and device status telemetry are robust, though carb entries are entirely absent.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 CGM entries spanning 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-21; 6214 device statuses; 2315 treatments; 0 carb entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of manual carbohydrate log entries.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range is 5.1%, exceeding the standard <4% safety threshold. Late-night/early-morning dipping and moderate afternoon hyperglycemia spikes (150-162 mg/dL local) require careful management.
analysis_steps.evidence: Time in range 86.0%, time above range 8.9%, time below range 5.1%, CV 32.6%, glucose extremes reaching 41 mg/dL low and 293 mg/dL high.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal carb data makes it challenging to separate postprandial peaks from baseline insulin tuning.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates combined with a strict 90 mg/dL target lead to nocturnal dipping and hypoglycemia (11%-18% time below range in hours 00:00-02:00 local).
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose averages at 00:00 (93.3 mg/dL, 11.4% <70) and 01:00 (90.6 mg/dL, 18.5% <70); active targets set to 90 mg/dL overnight.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Overlapping evening correction IOB and unlogged evening intake.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U across all segments. With zero logged carbs, AAPS relies entirely on Dynamic ISF (70% factor) and UAM/SMB automation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Static ISF 56 mg/dL/U, CR segments 10.5-13.2 g/U, DIA 10 hours, 655 insulin entries, 0 carb entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of logged carbohydrate data prevents empirical audit of Carb Ratios.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are appropriately enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, allowing the closed loop to catch unannounced intake given zero manual carb entries.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, smb_interval=3 min, max_smb_basal=15 min, max_uam_smb_basal=20 min.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF is active at 70% adjustment factor while autosens is disabled. Safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) provide a safe ceiling for automated dosing.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70%, max_basal=12 U/h, max_iob=25 U.

analysis_steps.findings: Meals are unannounced and unbolused, leading to reactive UAM/SMB corrections that cause afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks followed by rebound hypoglycemia risk.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero recorded carb entries; therapy response windows show automated micro-bolus responses to positive glucose deltas.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of declared meal composition and carb amounts.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not utilized in telemetry; standard UAM absorption modeling with a 7-hour max absorption window manages unannounced intake.
analysis_steps.evidence: Extended carb entries = 0; meal_max_absorption_hours = 7 h; min_5m_carbimpact = 8 mg/dL/5 min.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No extended or e-carb treatments recorded.

analysis_steps.findings: The system achieves solid glycemic control (86% TIR) via aggressive automation, but elevated time below range (5.1%) and nocturnal dipping indicate that the overnight target (90 mg/dL) and late-night basal rates are slightly too aggressive. Manual carb entry is absent, making UAM reliance necessary but prone to postprandial spiking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined telemetry showing 5.1% <70 mg/dL, 8.9% >180 mg/dL, zero carb entries, and active closed-loop parameters.

strengths: High CGM coverage (98.7%) with stable overall Time in Range (86.0%).
Robust AAPS closed-loop automation with SMB and UAM correctly enabled to handle unannounced intake.
Well-configured safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) supporting closed-loop operation.
issues: Time below range (5.1%) exceeds the standard 4% safety threshold, driven by nocturnal and early-morning dipping.
Afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks (averaging 150-162 mg/dL local from 13:00 to 17:00) resulting from entirely unannounced meals.
Flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U forces heavy reliance on Dynamic ISF and reactive UAM/SMB stacking.

recommendations.title: Adjust Overnight Target
recommendations.description: The 90 mg/dL target from 00:00 to 08:00 contributes to an 11%-18% hypoglycemia rate in early night hours. Raising the overnight target slightly can reduce nighttime lows.

recommendations.title: Introduce Meal Carb Logging
recommendations.description: Logging carbohydrates for a subset of meals will allow AAPS to utilize predictive dosing rather than relying exclusively on reactive UAM/SMB detection.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight time below range reaches 18.5% at 01:00 local time under the strict 90 mg/dL target. Raising the overnight target segment from 90 mg/dL to 95 mg/dL will improve safety without sacrificing overall control.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight CGM trends for 7 days after adjusting the target to confirm reduction in time below 70 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Increase the 00:00 target segment low and high from 90 mg/dL to 95 mg/dL.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies entirely on unannounced meals (UAM) and SMB automation without manual carb logging. While AAPS successfully manages blood glucose, this reactive approach leads to afternoon postprandial elevation and rebound hypoglycemia risk.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain active SMB and UAM automation, and consider manually logging carbohydrate entries for a subset of meals to enable predictive insulin dosing and smooth out postprandial spikes.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor postprandial glucose peaks and time-in-range when manually logging carbohydrates for representative meals over a 3-day test period.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review the recommended overnight target change (from 90 mg/dL to 95 mg/dL for the 00:00 segment) with the care team.
Step 2: Apply the target adjustment and monitor nocturnal and early-morning CGM readings for one week.
Step 3: Evaluate introducing manual carb entry for representative meals to assess whether predictive dosing improves postprandial time-in-range.
education: Unannounced meal (UAM) handling relies on positive glucose deltas to trigger automated micro-boluses, which inherently creates a time delay resulting in postprandial peaks.
Raising nighttime targets slightly can provide a helpful buffer against nocturnal hypoglycemia without compromising overall glycemic control.
